data.gender_notes: Srikanta is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who holds the wealth of the universe in his hands. The name Srikanta carries the meaning “Lord of Wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Srikanta usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Srikanta belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Wealth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Srikanta total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rama, derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ramah' meaning 'pleasing to behold', created a profound influence in Indian culture as it is often associated with love, morality, and heroic values. Rama's epic story is one of the most famous tales in India.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Rama is revered as an avatar (divine incarnation) of the god Vishnu. The story of Rama teaches important spiritual values, such as duty, selflessness, truth, and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Srikanta, meaning "Lord of Wealth", embodies the divine aspect of abundance and prosperity. His name symbolizes the attainment of material and spiritual wealth through the grace of the divine.

historical_references.reference: According to the 'Skanda Purana', Lord Srikanta is an incarnation of Lord Vishnu and is also known as Hari-Kanta. He is worshipped in the form of a deity holding a conch and a discus. The name Srikanta is derived from the Sanskrit words 'shri', which means wealth or fortune, and 'kanta', which means a lover or a beloved. Srikanta is often depicted as the lover of Goddess Lakshmi.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, possibly 6th century CE or earlier

historical_references.reference: In the 'Mahabharata', there is a reference to a sage named Srikantha who was a disciple of the sage Vyasa. He is known for his extreme devotion towards Lord Krishna and is often recalled in the context of the great epic. The name Srikantha can be interpreted as one who is dear to Lord Shri or Wealth, reflecting the sage's deep spiritual wealth and connection to the divine.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, possibly 4th century BCE or later

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern times, the name Srikanta is seen on various platforms as a symbol of devotionalism, spirituality, and self-help. On social media, individuals may use the name as a handle to express their religious or spiritual beliefs. On blogging websites, there are numerous blogs dedicated to the life and teachings of Lord Srikanta. Podcasting apps also host podcasts that discuss the legends and teachings associated with the name. Overall, Srikanta is a name that resonates with individuals seeking spiritual growth and connection to their beliefs.
